backfill.notes: Each idempotent backfill visits only the finite set of pre-existing groups, expenses, ledgers, balances, or links and writes rows whose new value is missing. A failed transactional attempt can be retried without duplicating settings.

locking.notes: ALTER TABLE and foreign-key validation take bounded locks; existing-row scans and index builds must complete within the normal migration timeouts.

rollback.notes: The previous application continues using the retained groups.currency field. Reversing the schema discards multi-currency settings and explicit accounting currencies.

backfill.notes: All users begin without grants, so the additive table requires no backfill.

locking.notes: Creating an empty table and its index does not rewrite existing user rows.

rollback.notes: The previous application ignores the additive table. Reversing the schema discards feature-grant state.

backfill.notes: The idempotent backfill visits the finite set of existing item rows, copies legacy values into the confirmed contract, and assigns stable positions by expense and item ID.

locking.notes: ALTER TABLE and the unique partial index take bounded locks; the existing item table is expected to remain small enough for the normal migration window.

rollback.notes: The previous application continues using retained and widened legacy columns. Reversing the schema discards confirmed line totals and ordering, and narrowing fails when new values do not fit the legacy contract.

backfill.notes: Existing expenses have no retained receipt association.

locking.notes: The new table and its indexes do not rewrite existing expense rows.

rollback.notes: The previous application ignores this additive table. Reversing it discards receipt association and cleanup state.

backfill.notes: An effective-category view projects single-category historical expenses without rewriting their rows.

locking.notes: Creates an empty child table, its uniqueness constraints, and a view. Foreign-key setup takes brief locks on expense and expense_type without a historical-row backfill.

rollback.notes: After multi-category writes, an older application cannot preserve or report those allocations. Keep this application version or restore compatible handling before rollback. Reversing the schema discards category amounts and notes.

backfill.notes: No historical rows are rewritten at installation. Registered cleanup triggers restrict future updates to one expense; repeated cleanup is idempotent.

locking.notes: Creates empty tables and bounded foreign-key metadata locks without rewriting existing rows.

rollback.notes: Older code ignores these tables. Schema reversal discards consent and evidence tracking; purge objects before any reversal.
